blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once met Hadhrat Hudhayfah bin Yamaan (RA) and was going to shake his hand, Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) turned away saying, "I am in a state of impurity." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "When a Muslim meets his brother Muslim and shakes his hand, their sins are shed off just as leaves are shed off a tree."[^2]
Narrations of Hadhrat Anas (RA) and Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) Concerning the Practice of Rasulullaah ﷺ With Regard to Embracing and his Prohibition from Bowing

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that the Sahabah (RA) once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Can we bow to each other (when greeting)?" "No," came the reply. They then asked, "Can we then embrace each other?" When Rasulullaah ﷺ again said "No", they asked, "Can we then shake each other's hands?" This time, Rasulullaah ﷺ's reply was "Yes".[^3]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that someone once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! When any of us meets his brother or his friend, can he bow to him?" "No," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Can he then embrace him and kiss him?" the Sahabi (RA) asked further. Again, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No." He then asked, "Can he then take his hand and shake it?" "This he may do," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ.[^4] Another narration adds that when the Sahabi (RA) asked, "Can he then embrace him and kiss him?" Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No, unless he has returned from a journey."[^5]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was in my house when Zaid bin Haaritha (RA) arrived in Madinah. When Zaid (RA) came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ and knocked at the door, Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up (in great excitement), dragging his clothing along with him but without wearing anything (over his upper body). By Allaah! I have never before or ever after seen Rasulullaah ﷺ like this. Rasulullaah ﷺ then embraced Zaid (RA) and kissed him."[^6]
The Practice of the Sahabah (RA) With Regard to Shaking Hands and Embracing
Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "It was the practice of the Sahabah (RA) to shake hands when meeting each other and embracing when returning from a journey."[^7]
Ahmad and Rooyaani, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.54).
